categories.rationale: Credential collection inventory is durable but its sensitivity, pagination, and ownership semantics require a separate resource decision.
Vector-store inventories and alternate durable CRUD surfaces require a separate identity and ownership decision.
JWT mapping records require dedicated stable identity, import, and deletion semantics.
Configured pass-through endpoint records can contain routing and secret-bearing data and need an explicit lifecycle design.
Policy records, versions, and many-to-many attachments require independent import, replacement, and drift semantics.
MCP toolset records and assignments have identities distinct from supported MCP server lifecycle ownership.
Per-user MCP credentials and environment records are durable sensitive configuration with separate ownership semantics.
MCP submission inventory is a durable management surface not covered by the supported server resource lifecycle.
Customer and end-user records overlap external identity systems and require explicit authority and import decisions.
SCIM users and groups are synchronization records whose source of authority cannot be assumed by Terraform.
Global proxy, integration, router, discount, and secret-backend settings have shared merge and restart semantics not modeled by current resources.
Callback, email, plugin, and marketplace plugin configuration requires dedicated identity and sensitive-value lifecycle review.
Alternate model and router management operations are not covered by the provider's reviewed model lifecycle.
Alternate key aliases and key-management records require separate ownership and import semantics.
Alternate team bulk and membership management operations are outside the supported resource lifecycle contract.
Alternate organization and project management operations require separate lifecycle and authority review.
Additional durable user, budget, tag, and allowlist configuration is not owned by current resource lifecycles.
Alternate access-group and unified access-control records require distinct identity and assignment ownership review.
Additional guardrail definitions and submission records are durable but not covered by the supported guardrail lifecycle.
Alternate agent, prompt-info, and tool definition operations are durable surfaces outside current lifecycle ownership.
Workflow and memory records require separate stable identity, import, and retention semantics.
Inference, pass-through forwarding, embeddings, media, MCP execution, and workload APIs execute requests rather than declare provider-owned configuration.
One-shot reset, migration, approval, cancellation, publication, and export actions have no durable Terraform identity.
Health, readiness, connectivity, and runtime status probes report operational state rather than desired state.
Spend, usage, logs, audit, activity, and analytics routes expose observations or one-shot calculations rather than durable configuration.
Cache deletion and flush routes are one-shot runtime actions with no durable identity.
Discovery, schema, comparison, resolution, marketplace, and suggestion routes return advisory or derived data.
OAuth, token, registration, callback, and well-known routes participate in runtime authentication protocols.
Dry-run, validation, conversion, compliance-check, and test-connection routes perform transient checks.
Public catalogs and available-object metadata are observational discovery surfaces.
Debug and control-plane log ingestion routes are runtime observability surfaces.
